Class Ppo

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.Ppo
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class Ppo extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Clipped-surrogate PPO with a separate critic. Each minibatch is split across a few low-priority worker threads, each with its own activations and gradient buffers.

    • selfImitate

      public Ppo.SilStats selfImitate(SilBuffer buf, Random rng, int batches, float weight, float valueWeight, float clip)
      Self-imitation (Oh et al., 2018), after a PPO update: of the kept steps that the critic still expects less of than they brought (R - V > 0), batches minibatches drawn at random, each step's action made likelier in proportion to that gap (clipped at clip), and the critic raised towards the return by valueWeight of it. Steps the critic has caught up with weigh nothing, so what is learned from them stops by itself.

    • update

      public UpdateStats update(Rollout r, Random rng, boolean trainActor, float entropyScale, float actorNeeds)
      Parameters:
      actorNeeds - the least share of the batch's returns the critic has to explain for the actor to learn from it; below that only the critic is trained. What the actor learns is "better or worse than the critic expected", and from a critic that expected nothing like what happened that is noise.

    • setTaskNormalisation

      private void setTaskNormalisation(Rollout r, float advMean, float advStd)
      With Config.taskAdvantageNorm, each kind of fight's advantages are normalised by their own mean and spread (PopArt's point, Hessel et al. AAAI 2019: in one network learning many tasks, the tasks with the biggest rewards drown the rest; here the fights against the no-knockback bot and the punisher move two to three times the damage of a spacer fight). A kind with fewer than TASK_NORM_LEAST steps in the batch is normalised with the whole batch.
